successCriteria.description: Both read paths (`ILeaveService.list` and `getById`) return rows that still carry `reversesRequestId` — null on ordinary rows, the original's id on a reversal row — with no field stripped from the entity.

Every returned row whose status is APPROVED carries a derived `isReversed` boolean (true when a reversal row exists for it, false otherwise), resolved at read time; rows in any other status (DRAFT/SUBMITTED/REJECTED/CANCELLED) carry no `isReversed` property at all. A single `getById` of an APPROVED request reports `isReversed === true` without the caller issuing a second query.

`list` returns BOTH the original APPROVED row and its CANCELLED reversal row by default (no rows hidden), and when `excludeReversals` is true it returns only rows whose `reversesRequestId` is null (the reversal row is filtered out).
The wire query parser accepts `excludeReversals` as the strings `'true'`/`'false'` and rejects any other value with a ValidationError (400); the parsed boolean reaches `leaveService.list`.

`npm run smoke` against real Postgres (SMOKE_DATABASE_URL set) passes the new GP-008 stages: after create → submit → approve → cancel-as-manager/ADMIN, (a) GET /leaves/:id for the original id returns status APPROVED with isReversed === true, (b) a new row exists with status CANCELLED and reversesRequestId === originalId, (c) GET /leaves returns both rows by default and only the original with excludeReversals=true, (d) the balance usedDays returns to its pre-request value (0) and available to 25 — released exactly once, not double-released. New stages are gated to Postgres mode with the existing sqlite caveat.
`tsc` is clean and the full Jest suite is green with no changes required to existing tests (widening the read return type is backward-compatible).

constraints: `isReversed` is DERIVED at read time only — never stored, never a column, never added to `LeaveRequest`/`CreateLeaveRequestInput`/`UpdateLeaveRequestDto`, and never written by any repository. The approved row remains byte-identical in storage (GP-007).
`list` and `getById` stay read-only: no `uow.withTransaction`, no client forwarding, no writes, no audit records, no notifications. The derived flag and the filter are pure read-time transformations.

`excludeReversals` is applied in the service as a post-filter after `repository.findByQuery`; the repository is NOT modified and silently ignores the field. A code comment must state that the repository ignores the field and that an unfiltered count double-counts a reversed request.
`excludeReversals?: boolean` is declared only in `LeaveRequestQueryParams` in `src/shared/types/index.ts`; no local duplicate DTO is declared in the leave module.
No new endpoints, no controller layer, no new named read-model type. `GET /leaves` and `GET /leaves/:id` keep their existing conventions (`resolveActor` at the API boundary, `sendError` mapping).

The smoke test must not modify `EMP.manager_id` (stages 4/5 assert it is null); the approving/cancelling actor is seeded as an `employees` row with ADMIN role to satisfy the `approver_id`/`cancelled_by` FKs. The smoke request's `startDate` must be strictly in the future (UTC) so the cancel timing guard does not raise ConflictError.

No hardcoded secrets (no-hardcoded-secrets): the smoke actor's password hash is minted from `SMOKE_PASSWORD` as the existing stages do. No `any` (use `unknown` + guards). No direct DB access outside the repository layer.
outOfScope: Any change to `src/modules/leave/leave.repository.ts` — the repository is not in this phase's file set and must not be modified (no `excludeReversals` support added there).
Any change to the reversal write path (`LeaveService.cancel`/`reverse`), the migration, the model, or the balance/audit/notification semantics — those are Phases 1–3 and are fixed contracts.
New endpoints, a controller layer, a named read-model type, or a `REVERSED` status value — none are sanctioned.
Frontend/web-client consumption of `isReversed`/`excludeReversals`, and any change to role-scoped visibility rules.

entityInvariants.invariant: The read projection is `LeaveRequest & { isReversed?: boolean }`. `isReversed` is present (true|false) ONLY on rows whose status is APPROVED and is absent on all other statuses; it is derived at read time and never persisted. `reversesRequestId` is present on every returned row (null on ordinary rows, the original's id on a reversal row).

An APPROVED row's stored fields are never mutated by the read path; its status stays APPROVED forever and `isReversed` is a read-time derivation, not a stored state. The reversal row carries `reversesRequestId` (non-null) instead.

Gains an optional `excludeReversals?: boolean`. When true, rows with a non-null `reversesRequestId` are excluded from the result; when absent/false, both rows are returned. The field is a query DTO concern only and does not alter the entity.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Existing role-scoped visibility unchanged: EMPLOYEE sees own only, MANAGER own + direct reports, ADMIN all. Reversal rows inherit the original's employeeId and are visible under the same rules (not hidden).
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Read-only; no transaction, no client forwarding, no writes. Returns both rows by default; applies `excludeReversals` as a post-filter. Attaches `isReversed` to APPROVED rows only.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Existing visibility unchanged; a request the caller may not see returns the same NotFoundError (404) as one that does not exist.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Read-only; no transaction. For an APPROVED request, resolves and attaches `isReversed` so the caller needs no second query. NotFoundError when absent or not visible.

interfaceConstraints.operation: Wire query parsing for `excludeReversals` (existing parseQuery helper)
interfaceConstraints.authRule: Unchanged — resolveActor at the API boundary.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Accepts only the strings 'true'/'false'; any other value throws ValidationError → 400 via sendError. Parsed value is passed through to leaveService.list.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: `excludeReversals` must be declared on the canonical `LeaveRequestQueryParams` DTO (the module that owns it), not a local duplicate.

The derived `isReversed` must be resolved via the existing `findByReversesRequestId` read lookup (or an equivalent read-path lookup) — the same method the reversal guard uses — rather than a new query shape.

The read projection must extend the existing `LeaveRequest` entity (which already carries `reversesRequestId`) rather than introduce a new named read-model type; `reversesRequestId` must not be stripped from returned rows.

The smoke stages must follow the existing Postgres-mode stage conventions (knex against `knexfile.smoke_pg` with the per-run schema, `app.inject`, real-value assertions) and reuse the existing sqlite caveat gating.
The read-path behaviour must match the reconciled business rules 2 (list default both rows + excludeReversals flag) and 3 (derived isReversed on the original APPROVED row, never stored).

The read paths must not violate GP-007 (approved rows immutable) or GP-008 (release exactly once) — the derived flag is read-only and the smoke proof must show the original still APPROVED and the balance released once.

integrationPoints.why: The read path resolves `isReversed` through this existing lookup; the repository is not modified.
Owns the query DTO that gains `excludeReversals`; the routes parser and the service both consume it.
The wire boundary that parses `excludeReversals` and passes it to `leaveService.list`.
Hosts the end-to-end GP-008 proof against real Postgres, gated to Postgres mode.
